title: SpiceJet's troubles: cancellations, unpaid dues and a search for money
dek: How one of India's oldest budget airlines came to cancel one in five flights, what it owes, and how it plans to raise up to ₹5,500 crore.
bigLabel: Share of SpiceJet's scheduled domestic flights cancelled in September 2026, per DGCA data reported by Mint. The industry average was 1.15%.

glance.what: SpiceJet has been cancelling about one in five of its flights since August, according to official data. No SpiceJet flight left Mumbai for more than 12 hours from the evening of 17 November, stranding hundreds of passengers. It is down to 12 aircraft, three of them reportedly grounded, and media reports say it is behind on payments to suppliers, aircraft lessors and staff. It has not published financial results since the December 2025 quarter.
glance.why: Passengers face last-minute cancellations, long delays and slow refunds. The aviation minister said in September that the regulator was reviewing SpiceJet's operations and finances.
glance.next: SpiceJet's reply to the DGCA's show-cause notice is due around 24 November; none had been reported by 23 November. On 18 November its board approved raising up to ₹5,500 crore; shareholders and regulators still have to approve it, and no investors have been named. The BSE will suspend trading in its shares from 10 December unless it files overdue results by 7 December.

forYou: Booked on SpiceJet? Check your flight status on the day and keep proof of any cancellation or long delay. If SpiceJet cancels your flight, ask for a refund or a seat on another flight; DGCA rules set deadlines for airlines to pay refunds.

upcoming.label: 7 Dec
upcoming.text: Deadline for SpiceJet to file its overdue March and June quarter results

upcoming.label: 10 Dec
upcoming.text: BSE to suspend trading in SpiceJet shares if the results are not filed

next: Shareholders must approve the ₹5,500 crore fundraise; overdue results are due by 7 December to avoid a trading suspension.

events.title: A normal month: 1 in 70 flights cancelled
events.summary: Background: in January, SpiceJet cancelled 1.44% of its flights and 56.8% were on time, according to DGCA data. It carried about 592,000 domestic passengers.

events.title: Credit rating cut
events.summary: CareEdge Ratings lowers SpiceJet's long-term bank rating to B+, citing continuing losses, a weak financial position and tight cash flow.

events.title: Lessors move to take back four grounded jets
events.summary: The DGCA publishes notices to remove four grounded Boeing 737 MAX planes from SpiceJet's records after the companies that lease them asked for them back on 9 July. The planes had been idle for over a year.

events.title: One in five flights cancelled
events.summary: DGCA data shows SpiceJet cancelled 20.92% of its scheduled flights in August, against an industry average of 1.04%.

events.title: Minister: regulator reviewing SpiceJet
events.summary: Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu says the DGCA is carrying out an operational and financial review of SpiceJet, with safety and passenger disruption as priorities.

events.title: Market share falls to 0.6%
events.summary: In September, SpiceJet cancels 20.29% of flights and only 16.6% are on time at 10 major airports. Nearly two in five flights are delayed by more than two hours. Its domestic market share falls to 0.6%, below the regional airline Star Air.
events.differs: Mint reports about 73,000 passengers in September; The Week reports 7.3 lakh (730,000).

events.title: Filing shows small suppliers waiting to be paid
events.summary: In a half-yearly filing, SpiceJet reports that ₹63 crore of the ₹123 crore it owed to small businesses between April and September was unpaid for more than 45 days. The airline gave "invoice received late" as the reason for nearly every overdue entry.

events.title: A wave of cancellations
events.summary: Passengers report cancellations on routes including Mumbai–Bengaluru and Delhi–Pune. SpiceJet is reported to be cancelling 15 to 20 of about 65 daily flights, with delays of three to five hours.
events.differs: The Week reports that nearly a third of daily flights were cancelled in recent days.

events.title: Nine of 12 planes flying; staff say salaries are late
events.summary: Mint reports that only nine of SpiceJet's 12 aircraft are flying, with three grounded because the airline is struggling to pay lessors. Two employees tell Mint that salaries are delayed, some by more than four months; Mint says it could not verify this. SpiceJet has not commented.
events.differs: Free Press Journal, citing sources, reports that salaries have been unpaid since June 2026.

events.title: Dubai flights cancelled over unpaid dues
events.summary: Reports say SpiceJet passengers in Dubai were refused check-in over unpaid dues, reported at ₹36 crore, and four SpiceJet flights from Dubai were cancelled. SpiceJet says it has "adequate bank guarantee cover in place" and is in talks with Dubai authorities.

events.title: Board to consider raising money
events.summary: SpiceJet tells the stock exchanges that its board will meet on 18 November to consider raising fresh capital through shares, preference shares, debt or a share sale to institutional investors.

events.title: Stock exchange warns of a trading halt; SpiceJet promises results by 7 December
events.summary: The BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange) says in a notice issued on Monday that it will suspend trading in SpiceJet shares from 10 December, because the airline has not filed its results for the March and June 2026 quarters. The suspension will not happen if SpiceJet meets the listing rules by 7 December. On Friday SpiceJet says it will publish the overdue results by that deadline. A spokesperson tells Reuters: "The completion of audit has taken longer time and hence caused delay in filing of results." SpiceJet's last results, published in February, covered October to December 2025.

events.title: No SpiceJet departures from Mumbai for more than 12 hours
events.summary: No SpiceJet flight left Mumbai airport from 7 pm on Tuesday, and the halt was still going on more than 12 hours later, according to Aviation Jeta, Amar Ujala and Dynamite News. Hundreds of passengers, on domestic and international routes, were stuck overnight, and some protested at the airline's counter. Aviation Jeta, citing airport sources, says 12 scheduled departures from Mumbai had been cancelled by Tuesday. SpiceJet had not issued a statement or given a reason by Wednesday morning. Passengers say they were not told about the delays or new departure times.
events.differs: Only Aviation Jeta gives a number of cancelled flights (12, from airport sources); the other reports say only 'hundreds' of passengers were affected.

events.title: Board approves raising up to ₹5,500 crore
events.summary: SpiceJet's board approved raising up to ₹5,500 crore, in one or more rounds, through new shares, debt with warrants or other securities, the airline said in an exchange filing reported by Business Today, Angel One and Upstox. Routes could include a share sale to institutions (QIP), a rights issue or a preferential allotment. The board also approved raising the company's authorised share capital, the maximum it can issue, from ₹2,000 crore to ₹7,500 crore. Both need shareholder and regulatory approval. Chairman Ajay Singh said the fundraise is 'an important opportunity to rebuild the airline'. The board was told about talks with possible new investors and asked management to close them quickly; no investors were named. The shares rose 5% to ₹9.97, the daily limit.

events.title: About three in four SpiceJet flights at the top three airports don't operate
events.summary: Of 42 SpiceJet flights scheduled on Thursday at Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, 31 were cancelled or did not operate, about 74%, according to Business Standard's analysis of airport data. Delhi airport posted that 'due to operational challenges being faced by SpiceJet airline, some flights may be impacted'. Business Standard says SpiceJet carried about 73,000 domestic passengers in September, down from about 592,000 in January. SpiceJet and the DGCA did not respond to the paper.

events.title: DGCA issues a show-cause notice; shares hit the lower limit
events.summary: India's aviation regulator, the DGCA, has asked SpiceJet to explain why action should not be taken against it, PTI reports, citing a notice dated 17 November. A show-cause notice is a formal warning that gives a company a chance to respond before any penalty. According to the reports, the notice says SpiceJet 'has failed to submit a credible plan for return to service of the grounded aircraft' and that most of its fleet is grounded. It also cites cancellations, poor on-time performance, not flying its approved schedule, uncertainty over renewing mandatory insurance, and concerns raised by overseas regulators about unpaid service providers. SpiceJet has seven days to reply. Its shares fell 5%, the most allowed in a day, to ₹9.74 on the BSE, per Upstox. SpiceJet had not commented, and the BSE asked it for clarification.
events.differs: Reports based on PTI put SpiceJet's domestic market share at 0.6% in September against 1.2% in August; an earlier Business Standard report compares the September figure with 3.9% in January.

events.title: SpiceJet reported to be flying 10–15 flights a day, while tickets stay on sale for cancelled routes
events.summary: SpiceJet is flying about 10–15 flights a day, against about 66 a day in its winter schedule, the Free Press Journal reports. At least eight Delhi–Mumbai flights each way were cancelled from 19 to 21 November, and a Mumbai–Dubai flight that had not flown for about a week was still on sale, it says. Passengers quoted by the paper say refunds have not arrived 20 days after cancellation; DGCA rules require card refunds within seven days. More than 7,000 complaints are on the government's AirSewa portal, PTI reports, per Millennium Post. SpiceJet has not commented on the ticket sales. No public reply to the DGCA's show-cause notice had been reported by 23 November.
events.status: Reported · Free Press Journal, Millennium Post (PTI); passenger claims are allegations
